if: goods or services or both are received by a taxable person FOR CONSTRUCTION OF AN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY ON HIS OWN ACCOUNT
the property is not of the excluded description in the parenthesis
and this applies EVEN WHERE the goods or services are used in the course or furtherance of business
then: CONFLICT — both locally held sources block the credit, but describe the exclusion differently and this file resolves neither. Source A excludes 'plant OR machinery'. Source B excludes 'plant AND machinery' and adds an Explanation 2 deeming every reference to 'plant or machinery' to have always been a reference to 'plant and machinery'
note: The one-word difference is decisive. 'Plant and machinery' is a DEFINED expression in the Explanation to s.17 and excludes land, buildings, civil structures, telecommunication towers and outside-factory pipelines; 'plant or machinery' is undefined and, being wider on its face, has been the subject of litigation. Source B's Explanation 2 is expressed to override any judgment, decree or order to the contrary, and source B footnotes the substitution to Act 7 of 2025 with retrospective effect from 01-07-2017 and the new Explanation with effect from 01-10-2025. Which text governs a given period is a legal determination and is deliberately left open. What both sources agree on is the sting in the tail: business use does NOT save the credit. Section 17(5) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 16 and sub-section (1) of section 18', so this block defeats both the s.16(1) entitlement and the s.18(1) special-circumstances credit. Business use does not cure it.
